description:
Fragment from the bottom of a legal document written on parchment. Dated Ṣafar 261 AH = November/December 874 CE. This is therefore the oldest Arabic document in the Geniza and likely the oldest dated document in any language in the Geniza. Most of what is preserved consists of people's names. From l. 8 onward (and possibly beginning earlier in this fragment), all of the names are followed by the witness formula وكتب شهادته, in some cases written as a ligature (وكتبـشهادته). Requires further study. 

On the other oldest dated documents of the Geniza, see Eve Krakowski and Sacha Stern, “The ‘Oldest Dated Document of the Cairo Genizah’ (Halper 331)," Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society 31.3 (2021): 617–634.

Reused on verso for Hebrew piyyuṭ for Shemini ʿAṣeret.

Identified by Alan Elbaum in August 2026.
